A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InfAlign work. All 24 pages of v3 and 26 pages of v4, including their equations, figures, and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original PaLM-2 alignment experiments on Anthropic helpfulness, harmlessness, and Reddit summarization, plus reward-hacking experiments in Appendix D.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experiments and adds transformation comparisons, raw-reward results, and adaptive inference experiments in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The calibration, reward transformation, and PPO optimization steps in Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Rewind-and-Repeat evaluates the existing alignment method under another decoding procedure; it does not revise InfAlign-CTRL.

E1.justification: Both versions use Anthropic helpfulness and harmlessness and Reddit TL;DR summarization. The added experiments retain these data and task requirements; varying N and applying Rewind-and-Repeat change evaluation procedures on the existing helpfulness task.

E2.justification: The figure legends retain PPO, IPO, log-sigmoid reward transformation, BoNBoN, and BoND. The added comparisons use these same baselines; the additional exponential transformation is an InfAlign-CTRL variant.

E3.justification: V4 adds empirical Best-of-2 evaluation, comparisons using t=5, and expected raw reward as an additional metric. Appendix G introduces adaptive stopping at the base policy's per-prompt 85th-percentile reward, capped at 32 generations, and measures repetitions to the threshold. Existing experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.6 adds empirical transformation sensitivity across N=2,4,32, supplementing the existing analytical comparison. Figure 8 checks performance under raw rewards, and Appendix G examines adaptive inference quality and efficiency. The original reward-hacking analysis is retained.

E5.justification: Existing shaded result bands are retained, and added plots follow the same presentation practice. V4 adds no seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence levels, significance tests, or explanation of how the bands are calculated.

E6.justification: Figure 5 adds empirical results favoring t=5 for Best-of-2 and t=10 for Best-of-4. Figures 8 and 10 add raw-reward and adaptive inference outcomes. Section 5.1 newly reports judge accuracies of 77.7%, 77.0%, and 76.4%. The original benchmark, poisoning, and analytical plots remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The definitions, theorems, equations, and proofs in the main text and Appendices B–C are unchanged. The added footnote connecting the differentiability assumption to BoN and WoN points to existing Lemma 5 rather than introducing new mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the inference-time mismatch claim, reward-transformation framework, InfAlign-CTRL contribution, and reported 3–8% improvements. Added experiments support these claims without redefining their central scope.

C2.justification: V4 explicitly acknowledges disagreement between model judges and human preferences. It also discusses the task-dependent tradeoff between calibration cost and performance, and interprets the new transformation comparisons as evidence against overfitting to a particular N.

D1.justification: Appendix F newly discloses training steps equivalent to 80 epochs and estimates calibration at 29% of total training time using a 2:1 backward-to-forward FLOP ratio. These are additional disclosures; neither PDF establishes an increase in training budget.

R1.justification: V4 adds Lambert et al.'s RewardBench reference and Zhang et al.'s Backtracking Improves Generation Safety. It also clarifies attribution of standard win-rate optimization to prior work. The broader positioning and Appendix A remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V4 adds Section 5.6 and Appendix G, expands the judge and computational-cost discussion, and renames Appendix E to Additional experimental results. Other changes are limited wording, typo, contact, and publication-information edits.

P2.justification: V4 adds Figures 5, 8, and 10, relocates some existing figures, and adjusts the first-page arrangement. Existing benchmark and appendix plots are retained, with later figures renumbered; the overall document layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: V4 strengthens the empirical support for transferring analytically chosen transformations to real models and tests adaptive inference beyond fixed-size sampling. Newly disclosed judge accuracy and calibration cost improve transparency about evaluation reliability and practical expense. These are useful, bounded gains, with the main method, theory, and original evidence unchanged.
